criteria.given: a validator built with Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2026-10-20T12:00:00Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC) and a batch containing one otherwise-valid request whose requestedAt is 2026-10-20T12:00:01Z
criteria.then: the StageResult problems contain exactly one Problem with code ProblemCode.SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP, field "requestedAt", the request's requestId, inputIndex 0, null relatedRequestId/escalatedFrom/escalatedTo, and the request is NOT in StageResult.requests()

criteria.given: a validator built with a clock fixed at 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z
criteria.when: validating requests whose requestedAt is exactly 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z, or earlier (e.g. 2026-10-20T11:59:59.999Z)
criteria.then: no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem is reported and the requests are accepted; only an instant strictly after the clock instant (including 2026-10-20T12:00:00.000000001Z) is treated as future — there is no tolerance window

criteria.given: the clock instant is 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z
criteria.when: a request WR-1 with requestedAt 2026-10-21T08:30:00Z is validated
criteria.then: the problem message is exactly "WR-1 has requestedAt 2026-10-21T08:30:00Z in the future" (requestId, then " has requestedAt ", the Instant.toString() of requestedAt, then " in the future"), and it never mentions the input index

criteria.given: a request whose requestId is null or blank and whose requestedAt is in the future
criteria.then: a SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem is still reported with requestId null and message "Request has requestedAt <instant> in the future", in addition to the MISSING_FIELD problem for requestId

criteria.given: a request with requestedAt null, or with requestedAt supplied through invalidFieldsByIndex as an unreadable raw value
criteria.then: only MISSING_FIELD (respectively INVALID_VALUE) is reported for field "requestedAt" and no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem is produced, because the future check needs a parsed instant

criteria.given: a request that is missing equipmentId and also has a future requestedAt
criteria.then: both problems are reported for that input index, with the MISSING_FIELD problems (produced in field order requestId, equipmentId, priority, requestedAt, description) first and the SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem last for that request

criteria.given: a batch where a future-dated request is rejected
criteria.then: the validate StageTrace has in = batch size, out = number of accepted requests (the future-dated one excluded), and notes contain the sorted, index-free entry "WR-1 rejected: future requestedAt" (label "Request without id" when the id is blank), reusing the existing "<label> rejected: <reasons>" format with reasons joined by ", "

criteria.given: a batch containing two requests with identical content, one dated in the past and one dated in the future, processed by WorkRequestProcessor with a fixed clock
criteria.then: the future-dated request is rejected in the validate stage with SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP, it never reaches the deduplicate stage (no DUPLICATE problem and no priority escalation is reported for it), and the trace still has exactly three entries validate, deduplicate, prioritize

criteria.given: a batch containing several future-dated requests at different positions, shuffled repeatedly
criteria.when: process(batch) runs with the same fixed clock
criteria.then: the accepted queue, the problem list and the trace notes are identical for every ordering; the SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problems appear in the validate-stage block ordered by inputIndex

criteria.given: the clock is read for the batch
criteria.when: validate(List) or validate(List, Map) is called
criteria.then: clock.instant() is consulted once per call so every request in one batch is compared against the same instant

criteria.given: existing code and tests that call new WorkRequestValidator()
criteria.when: the class is compiled and used
criteria.then: the no-arg constructor still exists and behaves as if constructed with Clock.systemUTC(); a new constructor WorkRequestValidator(Clock clock) is added and throws NullPointerException with message "clock" when given null

criteria.given: the Spring application context
criteria.when: it starts with no overriding bean
criteria.then: ProcessingConfig exposes a java.time.Clock bean named clock returning Clock.systemUTC(), and the workRequestValidator bean is built with that Clock; no new configuration property is introduced

criteria.given: the ProblemCode enum
criteria.then: it contains SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP declared last (after CONFLICTING_REQUEST_ID), so existing constants keep their order, BatchObserver gets one counter per code including the new one, and ProblemDto serialises the code as the string "SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP" with field "requestedAt"

criteria.given: the pinned 13-request sample batch (all requestedAt on 2026-10-20) processed with the production system clock after 2026-10-20
criteria.then: no SUSPICIOUS_TIMESTAMP problem is produced and the pinned queue, problems and trace counts 13 → 10 → 6 are unchanged

outOfScope: Any configurable clock-skew tolerance or grace window (e.g. app.validation.future-tolerance); the check is strictly > now
Flagging suspiciously old timestamps or implausible date ranges
Accepting future-dated requests with a warning instead of rejecting them
Checking timestamps in the deduplicate or prioritize stages, or changing the sort order
Changing WorkRequestProcessor, DuplicateResolver, WorkRequestSorter or RequestMapper signatures or behaviour
Rewriting sample-batch.json to include a future-dated request
Per-sending-site clock diagnostics, aggregate clock-drift metrics, or new API endpoints/fields beyond the existing problem representation
Time-zone conversion or normalising requestedAt values
